quests.instruction: Choose the most appropriately cautious claim.
quests.prompt: A pilot with 30 staff found fewer late arrivals when hours were flexible.
options: The pilot suggests that flexible hours may reduce lateness.
The pilot shows that lateness is impossible under flexible hours.
Flexible hours obviously reduce lateness for all staff everywhere.
The pilot proves that flexible hours end lateness for good.
quests.hint: A pilot is a small trial, so the wording should match its size.
quests.explanation: 'Suggests' and 'may' fit a small trial. The others claim proof or universal results.

quests.instruction: Which sentence uses a suitable amount of hedging?
quests.prompt: Choose the sentence that is careful but still clear.
options: Later start times tend to improve alertness in teenagers.
Later start times always improve alertness in every teenager.
Later start times are related to being alert in some way.
Later start times might possibly perhaps have some effect, maybe.
quests.hint: Too much hedging makes a claim unclear; too little makes it absolute.
quests.explanation: 'Tend to' is careful but still says something definite. One option is over-hedged and one is absolute.

quests.instruction: Which sentence is over-hedged, making the claim unclear?
quests.prompt: Choose the weakest sentence.
options: The policy helps most new starters, according to the survey.
It could perhaps be argued that the policy may possibly help a little, in some ways.
The policy is likely to help new starters.
The policy may help new starters settle in more quickly.
quests.hint: Count the softening words.
quests.explanation: 'Could perhaps', 'may possibly' and 'in some ways' make the claim vague. The other choices are cautious but clear.

quests.instruction: Choose the most precise version.
quests.prompt: Original: 'The new system is better.'
options: The new system is much better in many ways.
The new system is a real improvement on the old one.
The new system works better than it did before.
The new system cuts booking time from eight minutes to three.
quests.hint: Precise writing says what improved and by how much.
quests.explanation: This version names the improvement and gives numbers. The alternatives repeat 'better' in different words.

quests.instruction: Choose the best revision.
quests.prompt: Original: 'Students need things to help them study.'
options: Students need quiet spaces and reliable Wi-Fi to study effectively.
Students need various resources to help them study.
Students need many things for study purposes.
Students need stuff that supports their studying.
quests.hint: Replace vague nouns with specific ones.
quests.explanation: 'Quiet spaces and reliable Wi-Fi' name the resources. The remaining options still use vague words.

quests.instruction: Choose the most precise word.
quests.prompt: 'Her feedback named two paragraphs and showed how to fix them. It was very ____.'
options: fine
specific
interesting
nice
quests.hint: Which word describes what made the feedback useful?
quests.explanation: 'Specific' describes feedback with details. The other words are general.

quests.instruction: Choose the revision that replaces exaggeration with evidence.
quests.prompt: Original: 'The bus is always late, and everybody hates it.'
options: The bus is late all the time, and people are furious about how badly the service is run.
The bus was late on four of five mornings this week, and several commuters complained.
The bus is never on time, and nobody in the whole town has a good word to say about it.
The bus is nearly always late, and most people are sick of waiting in the cold every morning.
quests.hint: Swap 'always' and 'everybody' for facts.
quests.explanation: This version counts the late mornings and reports complaints. The alternatives still use sweeping words.

quests.instruction: Which sentence avoids exaggeration?
quests.prompt: Describing the lunchtime queue.
options: The queue at lunchtime lasts for an eternity.
The queue at lunchtime is the longest in history.
The queue at lunchtime often reaches the door.
Nobody could survive the queue at lunchtime.
quests.hint: Choose the sentence that could actually be observed.
quests.explanation: The correct sentence describes something visible. The remaining options use extreme comparisons.

quests.instruction: Which revision keeps the point but removes the exaggeration?
quests.prompt: Original: 'This homework will destroy our weekend.'
options: This homework will kill us before Monday arrives.
This homework is the worst assignment ever set.
This homework will completely ruin our lives this weekend.
This homework will take most of our weekend.
quests.hint: The complaint about time can be stated without extreme words.
quests.explanation: 'Take most of our weekend' keeps the complaint but is believable. The alternatives exaggerate.

quests.instruction: Choose the best reply.
quests.prompt: Priya writes in the team chat: 'I think we should cancel the Friday stand-up.'
options: Cancelling the stand-up would be the dumbest thing we could do, Priya, and I hope nobody agrees with it.
Whatever you want is fine with me, Priya; it does not matter to me one way or the other.
I see why it feels repetitive, but it is our only regular chance to spot blockers. Perhaps we could shorten it instead.
You always want to cancel things, Priya, and it never seems to occur to you that others rely on them.
quests.hint: Good disagreement acknowledges the point and offers an alternative.
quests.explanation: The best reply understands the concern and suggests a compromise. The alternatives insult, give up or accuse.

quests.instruction: Choose the best reply to criticism of your proposal.
quests.prompt: A colleague writes: 'Your proposal ignores the cost.'
options: Cost is not the most important factor in this case, so I do not think we need to discuss it further.
Fine, I will just drop the proposal altogether, since it is obviously not going to satisfy anyone here.
Thank you for raising cost; I will add a budget section so we can compare it with the current process.
It does not ignore cost; you clearly did not read the proposal properly before sending your comments.
quests.hint: A strong reply uses the criticism to improve the proposal.
quests.explanation: The right reply accepts the point and offers a fix. The other choices argue defensively or give up.

quests.instruction: Which reply disagrees while keeping the relationship strong?
quests.prompt: A commenter says: 'Dress codes are outdated.'
options: I understand that view. In client-facing jobs, though, a consistent dress code can build trust.
You have obviously never met a client in your life, or you would not be saying anything like that.
Dress codes are here to stay in professional workplaces, so you may as well give up on this argument.
That is a naive thing to say about the workplace, and it shows how little you understand about business.
quests.hint: Acknowledge, then give a reason for your view.
quests.explanation: The best reply respects the view and adds a reason. The others insult or dismiss.

quests.instruction: Choose the most useful product feedback.
quests.prompt: You are writing to the makers of a mobile app.
options: The app is great, no changes needed, and I would recommend it to anybody who asks me about it.
The app is terrible and needs to be redesigned from the start, because nothing about it works well.
The checkout button is at the bottom of the screen, and it is grey with white text on the small phones.
The app is easy to navigate, but the checkout button is hard to find on small screens; moving it higher would help.
quests.hint: Useful feedback names what works, what does not and a fix.
quests.explanation: The correct feedback gives a strength, a problem and a suggestion. The others are too harsh, too vague or only descriptive.

quests.instruction: Choose the most constructive comment on a presentation.
quests.prompt: You are speaking to a colleague after their talk.
options: Your examples were clear; the slides might be easier to read with less text on each.
Your slides were too crowded and your talk was boring, so most of the room stopped listening early.
Great job, there is nothing to improve, and I would not change a single word if I were you.
I have seen better presentations from new starters, so maybe the slides need to be started again.
quests.hint: Constructive comments are specific and kind.
quests.explanation: The correct comment praises something and suggests one improvement. The remaining options insult or give no help.

quests.instruction: Which comment would help the writer most?
quests.prompt: A classmate reads your essay.
options: Your second paragraph makes a strong claim, but it needs an example to show why it is true.
Add more detail everywhere in the essay, because more detail makes any essay stronger.
Your second paragraph is weak, and it does not seem to be as strong as the others in the essay.
I really liked your essay overall, and I would be happy to read more of your writing in the future.
quests.hint: Helpful comments say where and what to change.
quests.explanation: The correct comment names the paragraph and the missing piece. The others are vague.

quests.instruction: Choose the most balanced and useful review sentence.
quests.prompt: A guest is reviewing a hotel.
options: I stayed at the hotel for three nights in March, and I arrived by train from the airport at noon.
The location was excellent and the staff were helpful, though the rooms were smaller than the photos suggested.
Small rooms, terrible value, and rude staff at the desk, so stay away from this place if you can.
The hotel is fantastic, perfect in every way, and I would tell everybody I know to book it right now.
quests.hint: A fair review includes details on good and bad points.
quests.explanation: The correct sentence gives strengths and one problem with specifics. The remaining options are one-sided or give no opinion.

quests.instruction: Which review sentence gives the reader the most helpful information?
quests.prompt: A customer is reviewing a tablet.
options: The battery did not live up to my expectations at all, and I found myself charging it every afternoon.
The battery is bad, and it was a big disappointment to me after all the praise in the advertisements.
Disappointing battery, and I would not recommend this tablet to anybody who wants to watch video.
The battery lasted about six hours of video, less than the twelve advertised.
quests.hint: Look for measurements and comparisons.
quests.explanation: This sentence tells the reader the result and how it differs from the claim. The alternatives only say it was poor.

quests.instruction: Which review is fair to a small business even though the writer had a problem?
quests.prompt: The order arrived late.
options: Late again. Typical of small shops, which never seem to care about deadlines or about their customers.
I have never had a worse experience anywhere, and I would tell all of my friends to avoid this shop.
My order arrived a week late, but the owner apologised at once and offered a discount.
The owner is clearly incompetent and should close the shop, since nobody can rely on it to deliver.
quests.hint: A fair review reports the problem and how it was handled.
quests.explanation: The correct review states the problem and the owner's response. The others attack or generalise.

quests.instruction: Choose the best opening for a sceptical manager.
quests.prompt: You want to propose a short trial of a new weekly schedule.
options: There is no point resisting this change, because the decision has already been made at a higher level.
We all want the team to finish projects on time, so I would like to suggest a small experiment.
Everyone else on the team already agrees with me on this, so there is little reason to wait longer.
You have been wrong about scheduling for years now, so I would like you to listen to me for once.
quests.hint: Start with something the reader also cares about.
quests.explanation: This opening shares a goal and proposes something modest. The remaining options accuse or pressure.

quests.instruction: Choose the best sentence for residents who oppose a new car park.
quests.prompt: You support the plan.
options: This plan will happen whether residents like it or not, so the best thing is to accept it now.
The plan is supported by most of the experts in the field, so residents should trust their advice.
Residents who disagree simply do not understand the plan, and a clearer leaflet would soon change their minds.
Like many of you, I care about keeping our street quiet, and that is why I support this plan.
quests.hint: Show that you share the residents' concern.
quests.explanation: This sentence finds common ground. The others dismiss, threaten or lean on authority.

quests.instruction: Which sentence acknowledges the reader's concern before giving evidence?
quests.prompt: You are proposing a trial to a cautious team.
options: Last year's pilot caused no missed appointments, so there is nothing to worry about and no need to discuss it.
You may worry that a trial will disrupt clients; last year's pilot caused no missed appointments.
Disruption is unlikely, whatever you may think about it, so the team should agree to the trial at once.
Clients rarely mind trials of this kind, so the team can take part without any special arrangements.
quests.hint: Name the worry, then respond with evidence.
quests.explanation: The correct sentence states the concern respectfully and then gives evidence. The others dismiss it.

quests.instruction: Which sentence uses a vivid, honest example to persuade?
quests.prompt: You want a shelter at a bus stop.
options: Only fools stand in the rain waiting for a bus, so the people who wait must be responsible for it.
Last winter, one mother waited forty minutes in the rain with a toddler because the stop has no shelter.
Everyone knows what winter is like, and nobody should have to stand at a bus stop in the cold.
Terrible things will happen if we do not act soon, and the council will be blamed for every one of them.
quests.hint: A good example is specific and true.
quests.explanation: The right sentence tells a specific situation. The alternatives are threats, generalisations or insults.

quests.instruction: Which rhetorical question supports the argument without pressuring the reader?
quests.prompt: You want to build a short walk into the working day.
options: Who would disagree with a walking break except a fool who has never felt tired at a desk?
Do you want to be the person who ruins the plan for everybody by refusing to try it out?
Are you really so lazy that you refuse to walk for five minutes in the middle of a busy day?
If a five-minute walk can clear our heads, why not build it into the working day?
quests.hint: A fair question invites thought without insulting anyone.
quests.explanation: This question links to a benefit and invites agreement. The remaining options insult.

quests.instruction: Which sentence uses a sensible comparison?
quests.prompt: You are promoting an app that costs £5 a month.
options: The app is better than every other app ever built.
The app is like a magic wand that fixes everything.
Paying £5 a month for the app costs less than one takeaway coffee.
Not buying this app is like throwing your money into the sea.
quests.hint: A useful comparison helps the reader judge the size or value.
quests.explanation: The correct comparison helps the reader see the cost. The remaining options exaggerate.

quests.instruction: Which sentence best suits customers?
quests.prompt: Explaining that a new billing system reduces errors.
options: Errors are reduced by half at the database level.
The system's validation rules reject invalid entries at input.
You will receive one clear bill each month, with fewer mistakes.
The system was implemented in the third quarter of this year.
quests.hint: Customers care about what changes for them.
quests.explanation: The correct sentence describes the benefit for customers in plain words. The rest are technical or internal.

quests.instruction: Which sentence best suits a technical colleague?
quests.prompt: Explaining that a new form reduces errors.
options: The form validates entries at input, so malformed dates are rejected before reaching the database.
We hope everyone enjoys the new look of the form, which uses the company's colours and a friendlier font.
You will find the form friendlier to use, because the boxes are larger and the instructions are clearer.
The form is simply better than the old one, and it has been welcomed by most of the staff who tried it.
quests.hint: A specialist wants to know how it works.
quests.explanation: The best sentence explains the mechanism. The other choices describe feelings or vague improvement.

quests.instruction: Which sentence best suits a manager deciding on a budget?
quests.prompt: Proposing the new form.
options: The form is used by other companies too, including several in our own industry that have adopted it.
Some staff already like the form, and several have said they would recommend it to their colleagues.
The new form should save about five staff hours a week, paying for itself within a year.
The form has a modern look and a pleasant layout, with clear headings and plenty of white space.
quests.hint: A budget-holder wants cost and benefit.
quests.explanation: The best sentence gives the saving and payback time. The remaining options describe appearance, opinion or popularity.

quests.instruction: Choose the best sentence for tone, precision and audience.
quests.prompt: You want neighbours to keep music down after 10 p.m.
options: Your music is unbearable and you clearly do not care about anyone else who lives in this building.
Noise should be lower at night in general, and neighbours should be considerate of each other.
Some neighbours have complained about noise before now, and the landlord has been made aware of it.
Would you mind keeping the music down after 10 p.m.? We have young children who wake easily.
quests.hint: A polite request gives a time and a reason.
quests.explanation: This sentence is polite and specific and explains why. The alternatives insult, generalise or blame.

quests.instruction: Which revision improves both tone and precision?
quests.prompt: Original: 'The website is awful and never works.'
options: The website is horrible and always broken.
The website is not very good, to be honest.
The website has problems at times.
The website failed to load on my phone three times today.
quests.hint: Replace judgement words with what actually happened.
quests.explanation: This version states specific events. The others are vague or extreme.

quests.instruction: Select the TWO sentences that adapt to a sceptical audience.
quests.prompt: You are presenting a new plan to doubtful colleagues.
options: I understand why some of you doubt the plan, so here is what the trial showed.
Those who doubt the plan simply have not read it, and they can catch up by reading the summary.
Doubters will be proved wrong soon enough, and we will all be able to look back on this and smile.
Let me start with the concern I hear most often: cost.
quests.hint: Choose sentences that treat doubt as reasonable.
quests.explanation: The correct sentences acknowledge doubts and address them. The remaining options dismiss or mock.
